content.ballot_question: Shall the office of the City Treasurer be appointive?
content.plain_language_summary: Walnut Creek currently elects its City Treasurer. Measure T would make it an appointed position chosen by the City Manager, who could set professional qualifications for the job.
content.yes_means: The treasurer would be appointed by the City Manager instead of elected, starting when the current term ends (December 2026, or December 2030 if a treasurer is elected this November).
content.no_means: Voters would keep electing the City Treasurer.
content.fiscal_impact: The City Attorney's analysis says approval would save future costs of candidate elections for the position.

argument_for.summary: Supporters say the job now oversees about $145 million and should require finance qualifications, noting that fewer than 10% of California cities still elect their treasurer.

argument_against.summary: Opponents say voters would lose direct choice of the official who reviews the city's own accounts, that voters rejected this in 1956 and 1996, and that savings would be minimal.

excerpts: Shall the office of the City Treasurer be appointive?

Measure T presents to the voters of Walnut Creek the question of whether the office of City Treasurer should be made an appointed position, with the City Manager having the authority to appoint the City Treasurer.
The City Manager ... would appoint the City Treasurer when the term of the current incumbent expires in December 2026 or ... in December 2030
If a simple majority of voters vote “NO” on this measure, the office of City Treasurer in the City of Walnut Creek will continue to be elected by voters.
If a simple majority of voters vote “YES” on this measure
this measure would save future costs associated with candidate elections related the position of City Treasurer.
ARGUMENT IN FAVOR OF MEASURE T
fewer than 10% of California’s 483 cities still locally elect their city treasurers
ARGUMENT AGAINST MEASURE T
Walnut Creek voters have weighed this question before and rejected it, in 1956 and again in 1996.
MEASURE T CITY OF WALNUT CREEK

content.ballot_question: Shall the measure amending the City of Walnut Creek General Plan, the North Downtown Specific Plan, and the Municipal Code to redesignate a 2.4 acre site at the northeast corner of North California Boulevard and Ygnacio Valley Road from office uses to mixed use residential uses, and to create a new Mixed Use Residential Senior & Commercial zoning district to limit allowable uses on the site to multifamily senior housing (primarily 55 years of age or older) and commercial uses compatible with senior housing, be adopted?
content.plain_language_summary: A citizen petition put this on the ballot. It would rezone a 2.4-acre office site across from Walnut Creek BART for housing mainly for people 55+, plus compatible shops. It does not approve a specific project.
content.yes_means: The site is rezoned for senior housing and compatible commercial uses, and the city could not substantively reduce that zoning later without another vote or the landowner's request.
content.no_means: The site keeps its current office designation.

argument_for.summary: Supporters say seniors make up a large share of nearby households but few planned homes are reserved for them, and that the measure would allow 200+ senior homes near BART without raising taxes.
signers: Marlene R. Farrell, Friends of Walnut Creek Senior Housing
Stephen L. Kostka, Advocate for Senior Housing
